passage: Gurpreet's thumb had opened Nirmala's profile before he even decided to. Same photos, one new story about a rainy bus stop. He looked at it for the ninth time that evening, and the algebra on his desk stayed untouched. His mind kept circling like a fan: what did the rain mean, why hadn't she liked his comment, who was in the picture. When he thought of cycling past her lane "just to see", something in him went cold, because that felt wrong. He shut the phone in the drawer and called his cousin Harsh instead. "It's like being hungry for something that never fills me," he said. Harsh laughed kindly and said, "Come to the badminton court. Bring your racket, leave the phone." Gurpreet smashed shuttles until his arm ached, and it felt good.

qa.q: What did Gurpreet do with his phone when he thought of cycling past Nirmala's lane?
qa.a: He shut it in the drawer and called his cousin Harsh.

qa.q: What does Gurpreet feel when he keeps checking her profile, and how can you tell?
qa.a: A restless hunger. He says it is like being hungry for something that never fills him, which shows he sees it as a loop that feeds itself.

qa.q: What steps helped Gurpreet in this passage?
qa.a: He put the phone away, talked to Harsh, and used his energy on the badminton court instead of checking or turning up at her lane.

qa.q: How might Nirmala see it if he had cycled past her lane uninvited?
qa.a: She would probably feel uneasy or watched, even if he meant no harm, so staying away respects her space.

grounding: Gurpreet checks his crush's profile constantly and cannot focus, and limits the checking, talks to a cousin and channels his energy elsewhere.

passage:
"Jomon, you've checked your phone eleven times in this chapter."
"I'm not checking. I'm just seeing."
"Seeing Merin's profile."
"She posted a story from her cousin's place. What if she's with someone?"
"Bro. Look at me. How much have we done tonight?"
"Half a page."
"And the test is Monday. You're stuck in some loop."
Jomon rubbed his face. "It's like I'm hungry for it. Every time I check, I feel good for one second, then worse."
"So let's fix it. Give me the phone till nine."
"What if she messages?"
"Then she'll wait. And don't even think about going to her tuition centre tomorrow to 'bump into' her."
Jomon went red. He had thought about it. "Okay. Take it."
Sahil put the phone in his bag. "After the test, you come to badminton with me. You need somewhere else for all this energy."

qa.q: How many times had Jomon checked his phone during the chapter?
How does Jomon describe the feeling of checking Merin's profile?
qa.a: He feels a kind of hunger; each check gives one second of feeling good and then leaves him feeling worse and anxious.

qa.q: Which steps could help Jomon break the loop?
qa.a: Handing his phone to Sahil until nine, not going to Merin's tuition centre, and putting energy into badminton after the test.

qa.q: How does Sahil see Jomon's checking?
qa.a: Sahil sees it as an unhealthy loop hurting Jomon's studies and cares enough to step in firmly but kindly.

grounding: A teen who keeps checking his crush's profile recognises the loop, limits checking with a friend's help and channels energy elsewhere.

passage:
Last spring I was Aparna, the girl who checked Manoj's profile about forty times a day. I'm not exaggerating. Before school, in the bathroom, under the desk. If he posted a photo, I zoomed in to see who else was there. If he didn't post, I kept refreshing.
My marks dropped in two subjects. I couldn't read a page without my hand reaching for my phone.
One night I caught myself planning to walk past his building "by chance." That scared me. It wasn't a crush anymore. It was a hunger that was eating everything.
I told my friend Zeenat the next day. She didn't laugh. She helped me mute his account and set my phone to lock social apps after eight.
I joined the school's Saturday pottery class, mostly to keep my hands busy. It worked better than I expected. I still like Manoj. I just don't live inside his profile anymore.

qa.q: How many times a day did Aparna check Manoj's profile?
What made Aparna scared about her own behaviour?
qa.a: She felt frightened when she caught herself planning to walk past Manoj's building, realising the crush had become an all-consuming hunger.

qa.q: Which steps helped Aparna, and why?
qa.a: Telling Zeenat, muting Manoj's account, locking apps after eight and joining pottery class broke the checking loop and gave her energy somewhere else.

qa.q: How might Zeenat see Aparna's confession?
qa.a: Zeenat seems caring and practical, taking it seriously without laughing and helping Aparna make changes.

grounding: A teen caught in a loop of checking a crush's profile recognises it, talks to a friend, limits checking and channels her energy elsewhere.
